title: Remove observation proof that the typed page entry duplicated

intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage: SEED-413#remove-observation-proof-overlap

Verdict: Caught. The maintained assertion caught the fault, but only on the path described below.

Story and revision: SEED-413#remove-observation-proof-overlap, checked at 1cecc12316fbf86eee1cc718ac6eaa4e5999efa3. That is the delivery commit. It removed the E2E case "a watched branch move reads only that entry's plan and commit time; the other page reads nothing further" from e2e/observation/revision-stream.spec.ts.

Promise: when a watched story branch moves and trunk stays still, the dashboard reads only that entry's plan content and plan commit time at the new head, and nothing else.

Fault chosen (I changed the caller's suggestion):
- First attempt, following the suggestion in dashboard/src/progressSource.ts (withProgressSources): unmoved story-branch entries were reread at their shown heads. A temporary console witness showed the fault running in the E2E journey: story/plan-missing@f3… and story/uninterpretable@f4… were reread. In Vitest it ran only for story/vanished, which has no head, so the faulted path never ran there.
- Even so, the fake GitHub call log for that step still held only the two expected on-branch reads. Those per-head reads are answered without a new upstream call, so the fault caused no wrong behavior anyone could see. I dropped it as a non-observable fault, with no verdict.
- Fault used instead: dashboard/src/requestedRead.ts (carryOutRead). I changed `if (movedBranches !== undefined && shown !== undefined)` to `if (false && …)`. A watched-branch move then rereads the whole snapshot instead of calling readMovedProgress. This is the caller's other suggestion ("reread a whole snapshot"). It sits one level up from readMovedProgress, at the point that decides between a moved-branch read and a full read.

Independent witness of the wrong behavior: a scratch copy of the journey, deleted afterwards. It printed readsBesideChecks for the moved step before any assertion ran. Under the fault the page made eight reads at the boundary:
- ref main
- content .planning/open-dough.json@d4…
- branch story/example, story/plan-missing, story/uninterpretable
- the on-branch plan content and commit-list @e6…
- commit-list 092-plan-missing/PLAN.md@f3…

Only the two on-branch reads @e6… should have happened.

Maintained checks examined:
- e2e/observation/auto-refresh-branches.spec.ts, step "a new slice commit on the recorded branch shows its count and a restarted clock within the check pace, reading only its plan and commit time there". Its assertion `expect(readsBesideChecks(callsSince(page, from)).sort()).toEqual([content …on-branch…@movedHead, commit-list …on-branch…@movedHead])` (line 119) failed, receiving the six extra reads above. **This is the assertion that caught the fault.**
- dashboard/frontend-tests/observation/moved-branch-progress.spec.ts, "a moved head rereads only the affected branch and clock". It passed under the fault. It calls readMovedProgress directly, so it never runs the faulted dispatch in requestedRead.ts. It gives no verdict for this fault; it is neither a catch nor a gap.

Reach and baseline: both focused commands passed at the unmodified revision. The E2E run was confirmed by an OPEN_DOUGH_E2E_PROOF_RECORD: selectedCount 1, that journey's test at line 71, outcome "expected". Vitest showed 2 passed.

Restoration: the fault was undone by copying the file back from a saved original, with a shell trap as backup. git status --porcelain was empty and HEAD was still 1cecc1231. Both focused commands were rerun and passed: E2E exit 0 with proof-record outcome "expected", Vitest 2 passed. The scratch worktree /Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/22ce6323/tmp/ic-scratch was then removed.

Limits of the claim:
- The catch covers the E2E journey's single-tab path, where a branch move is dispatched into a full snapshot read.
- The removed case's second-tab half is not covered by this probe: two tabs sharing a context clock, with the other page reading nothing further.
- A fault that rereads unmoved branch entries at the same heads causes no extra GitHub reads. It cannot be seen at this boundary, so neither maintained check is expected to catch it.

Next proof action: none needed for this promise on the probed path. To cover the second-tab half, a separate probe would have to fault the shared-context path.

Prior disposition: this matches the delivery commit's claim that auto-refresh-branches and the moved-head Vitest case carry the watched-branch move. The probe shows that for this fault the E2E step carries it and the Vitest case does not reach it. No repair decision follows from this probe.

Cost:
- Test runtime: measured, from Playwright proof-record durationMs for the E2E test and the Vitest-reported Duration, wall-clock per run.
  - Baseline: E2E 5.6 s, Vitest 0.99 s.
  - Faulted: E2E 4.0 s (failed), Vitest about 1 s (passed). The witness spec run was about 5 s.
  - Restored: E2E 4.3 s, Vitest 0.62 s.
  - Total across about 8 focused runs: roughly 30 s, excluding npm ci.
- Human effort: unavailable; no human took part during the probe.
- Agent effort: unavailable; this agent has no token or time meter.

- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 217263 ms (measured), from 1795436327242 to 1795436544505 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

Wrap-up disposition: checked revision 1cecc12316fbf86eee1cc718ac6eaa4e5999efa3, verdict Caught, no follow-up.
